{{Short description|Type of pseudoprime}}
In [[number theory]], a [[pseudoprime]] is called an '''elliptic pseudoprime''' for (''E'',&nbsp;''P''), where ''E'' is an [[elliptic curve]] defined over the [[Field (mathematics)|field]] of [[rational number]]s with [[complex multiplication]] by an [[Order (ring theory)|order]] in <math>\mathbb{Q} \big(\sqrt{- d} \big)</math>, having equation ''y''<sup>2</sup>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''x''<sup>3</sup>&nbsp;+&nbsp;''ax''&nbsp;+&nbsp;''b'' with ''a'', ''b'' [[integer]]s, ''P'' being a point on ''E'' and ''n'' a [[natural number]] such that the [[Jacobi symbol]] (−''d''&nbsp;|&nbsp;''n'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;−1, if {{nowrap|(''n'' + 1)''P'' &equiv; 0 (mod ''n'')}}.

The number of elliptic pseudoprimes less than ''X'' is bounded above, for large ''X'', by

:<math> X / \exp((1/3)\log X \log\log\log X /\log\log X) \ . </math>
